question: What is the canonical control-plane action contract, and how do ActionChoice / RenderedEvent relate to it?
answer: ActionItem is the single canonical control-plane action contract. ActionChoice (operations_guidance.py) and RenderedEvent (event_copy.py) remain producer-specific inputs that project INTO ActionItem (via Guidance.to_action_items and _rendered_to_action_item_dict). No third action type may be introduced. dedupe_key is first-class. exact_command + automatable remains the command-safety model; there is no separate safe_command field.
rationale: Verification at HEAD c814cc9 showed all three types already triangulate into one contract via tested projections and provider-wins dedup in merge_with_event_sidecar. Formalizing rather than rebuilding.

question: How to reconcile the operations: (ActionChoice) vs supervisor: (RenderedEvent) id-prefix inconsistency, given both set source=supervisor?
answer: Keep _VALID_SOURCES closed and treat the id-prefix as opaque. Introduce an explicit dedupe_key field as the identity/dedup authority; do NOT derive dedup from id-prefix parsing. operations-guidance items continue to carry source=supervisor by design — documented, not changed.
rationale: id-prefix != source today (operations: and supervisor: both map to source=supervisor); dashboard_relevance already parses some ids by prefix, so a prefix-derived dedup key would be unreliable. An explicit dedupe_key removes the ambiguity without a risky source-vocabulary change.

question: Should the control-plane re-architecture expand 2026-05-30-001 or be a new plan, and what is in scope?
answer: New plan (this one) that REBASES on top of 2026-05-30-001 — which finishes F014 -> F011 -> F010 untouched. Scope is the spine ONLY: F001 ActionItem contract, F002 operator/worker/orchestrator honest classification, F003 renderer parity. Orchestration-tree governance (tree-aware budget/breakers, multi-writer undo/drift) is deferred to a demand-gated Plan B; the plan-quality recast stays with 2026-06-01-001.
rationale: 2026-05-30-001 is locked and one-feature-from-done; its objective_contract is built on the flat operator/worker model. Redefining the persona axis is a new-contract event per the scope-change protocol. Plan B is demand-gated (no real fan-out-harness dispatch exists yet) per demand-driven-v2 discipline.

question: When does orchestration-tree governance (Plan B) get built?
answer: Demand-gated: only after DontPanic actually dispatches to a fan-out-capable harness (a real can_orchestrate=true worker run exists). Until then F002 reports the can_orchestrate capability but does not act on it.
rationale: Building tree-aware budget/breaker/undo before a real orchestrating worker exists is speculative; scope the next increment on a real-world trigger, not up front.

question: Should Plan A add autonomy policy fields (policy_allowed, why_blocked) for the future autonomous-safe run loop?
answer: No (non-implementing forward-compat note). The ActionItem spine should ANTICIPATE future autonomy fields such as policy_allowed and why_blocked, but they are NOT part of Plan A. They belong to the later autonomous-safe run-loop / fleet-scheduler work, after ActionItem classification (automatable/requires_human/risk/reversible) is reliable. No feature change in this plan.
rationale: Recorded now to prevent two failure modes: (1) Plan A accidentally growing autonomy policy fields before any consumer exists; (2) the later run-loop plan churning the spine because the extension point was never recorded. Hard dependencies preserved: autonomous cross-feature run is DOWNSTREAM of Plan A; the agent brief must NOT instruct outer agents to continue automatically until the run-loop policy exists; budget reservation and a durable supervisor are shared prerequisites with the fleet scheduler. See memory project-autonomous-safe-run-loop.

question: How are the 9 pre-impl sufficiency findings (live codex audit, 1 critical / 3 high / 4 medium / 1 low) dispositioned before lock?
answer: Critical FIXED in-spec; the rest encoded-in-acceptance or routed to the implement->audit volley, then lock via --ignore-sufficiency-findings with this itemized disposition. (1) CRITICAL integration_gap [F001] — objective claimed 'no safe_command field exists anywhere' but safe_command is live in config_inventory.py (67 refs) + skill_recommendation.py: FIXED by narrowing objective_contract.json (journey signal + non_goal + completion_test) to 'no safe_command on ActionItem/the control-plane spine; pre-existing usage out of scope'. (2) high wiring [F001/F003] one shared ActionItem read path + parity test must fail if a surface recomputes: F003 acceptance already requires 'No renderer constructs ActionItems independently of the spine' — the implement->audit volley enforces the shared-loader + negative parity assertion. (3) high parity [F003] / (4) high coverage [F001]: acceptance already names parametrized all-producer-path coverage + dedupe_key dedup + boundary validation; sharper assertions are the auditor's job during the volley. (5)-(8) mediums [F001/F002/F003 coverage/integration/wiring] + (9) low: acceptance-sharpening, deferred to volley. No second sufficiency audit burned (one live codex call already run; one-paid-call discipline + operator-authorized full volley).
rationale: Live codex sufficiency audit (evidence/goal-governance/pre_impl/sufficiency-findings.json, ~1.5M tokens in / 12k out) surfaced one real structural defect (the safe_command over-claim) and eight acceptance-sharpening items. The gate's job is to catch cheap-to-prevent structural defects pre-impl; that one is fixed in the spec. The remaining items are exactly what the implement->audit volley enforces, so routing them there (rather than a second paid sufficiency audit) honors both the audit signal and the budget. Operator authorized: pay-for-real-audit (done) + full live volley across F001-F003.
